Details of Kshethram:
Moolavar: Parthasarathy Perumaal
Thayaar: Tamaranayaki Thayaar
Vimanam: Narayana Vimanam
Pushkarani: Kadga Theertham

Travel: This kshethram is located 10 km from Sirkazhi

Azhwar Pasuram: 
Tirumangai Azhwar: 10 Pasurams

Sthala Puranam:
The legend states that this temple was established by Arjuna during his trip to South India, when he was in vanavaasam with the Pandavas. It is said that when Arjuna reached this kshethram, he was extremely thirsty and went in search of water. When he could find no water, he found Agastya Maharishi performing tapas. Arjuna paid his respects to the Maharishi and asked him if he had any water. Agastya Maharishi said all the water he could offer was that which was there in his kamandalam. After Arjuna drank the water, he asked the sage if he could direct him to a source of water, as he was still thirsty. Agastya Maharishi said there was no water in the area and told Arjuna to seek the help of Lord Krishna, as he always did. Arjuna then performs tapas to call Lord Krishna to this kshethram. When Lord Krishna arrived, he gave Arjuna a sword and asked Arjuna to dig the earth. When Arjuna dug the earth, a stream of water emerged, granting water to the area. This water source came to be known as Kadga Theertham( the water that came from the sword).


***Here, one can see Lord Parthasarathy with four hands, as supposed to see him with two hands like at Tiruvallikeni(Chennai). Another specialty of this kshethram is that one can see the utsava moorthigal of both Lord Rama and Lord Krishna standing in the same garbha-graham. We can see Kolavili Ramar holding the shankam, chakram, bow, and arrow.
